quest.title: A Mysterious Visitor From Huitztlan
quest.description: You encounter two kids beneath the cliffs outside the Scions of the Canopy tribe. They seem to require some help...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Mora x27825, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Go beneath the cliffs outside the Scions of the Canopy's dwellings
Go beneath the cliffs outside the Scions of the Canopy's dwellings

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Hi! I'm Huni, are you here to help find the baby Saurians?

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: And I'm Toba. You must be the helpers that we've been waiting for!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... It's nice to meet you, too! But we were just passing through...

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: But Uncle Sanka said he was gonna send some of his friends over to help us... You sure he didn't mean you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm afraid we don't know anyone called Sanka.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, sorry... Whatever this is about, it sounds like you got the wrong end of the stick.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Wrong end of the stick?

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Darn it! We've been tricked, Huni! I should've known that glasses guy was a con artist...

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: What are we supposed to do about the baby Saurians now? Time's running out...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's okay, Huni, don't worry! Why don't you tell us what happened with these baby Saurians, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: There's been a lot of unrest in the tribe lately, and my dad's Saurian got injured... Her name's Nanna, and she has three little babies.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: After what happened to Nanna, her babies were so scared that they ran off and hid. I'm really worried about them, so I decided to go look for them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If Nanna is your dad's Saurian... Why isn't he the one looking for them?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: My dad's one of the elders, so he's busy getting ready for Turnfire Night. It's a really important ceremony — more important than this, anyway. I'm not supposed to be out here either, but I snuck out without telling him...

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: I didn't think it would take very long. But then that guy we ran into made us tell him loads of stories, and it wasted so much time...

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Yeah, he was so selfish! He doesn't have a heart!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #It's alright, don't let him get to you! We're here now, and we'll help you. Because we care a lot, don't we, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We sure do. So, are the baby Saurians nearby?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: They should be! I already managed to find their tracks, and it seems like they're hiding on the cliff...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave it to Paimon and me. It shouldn't take long.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: #Really? Wow... Thank you so much, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} {NICKNAME}, and Miss Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Awesome! You gotta be careful out on the cliffs, though. They're really steep. Even grown-ups have trouble climbing them.

dialogues.speaker: Ponini
dialogues.text: (Too high! I'm scared!)

dialogues.speaker: Poggi
dialogues.text: (The Mountain King...)

dialogues.speaker: Pocchi
dialogues.text: Awoo...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We found them! ...Wait, but what's that other... Ajaw!?

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Well, if it isn't the gruesome twosome, who wormed their way into our servant's circle of friends... Still awe-struck from the last time we met? Would that be why you hastily scrambled up here to pay your respects the moment you saw us? I suppose we can't blame you. Such is the spell that our majesty casts on our minions.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Very well! You heathens leave us no choice... the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw shall grant you the audience that you seek. Come. Pucker up. You may now kiss our feet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, aren't you like... Kinich's sidekick? What the heck are you going on about? You're somehow managing to be even more annoying than the last time we met.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Silence! Who are you calling "sidekick"? We are the dragon supreme! Sovereign ruler of the Nation of Flame!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: We shall have you know that last time, were it not for Kinich's earnest pleading on your behalf, you would have received not a single word of mercy!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, come on! You talk big, but Kinich clearly has you under lock and key!

choices.text: O great sovereign, what brings you to this mountaintop?

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: If you must know — our humble servant begged us to investigate an Abyss incident near Huitztlan, and we chose to grant his request.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: See this little lizard? Its mother, a medium-sized lizard, came under the influence of Abyssal power. In her confusion, she attacked my servant's tribe, then assailed her own offspring.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yikes... So how is she doing now?

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: She was but a lowly bug fighting against the power of the Abyss. Naturally, she has departed for the Night Kingdom.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Such a fragile creature... Apparently, she ended her struggle by leaping from a cliff.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: My dear Anemic Flying Ant, as addled with questions as your head may be, please keep them to yourself. And wipe that absurd expression off your face. We are the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw, not a wish-granting fountain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anemic Flying Ant!? You...! Just you wait, two can play at the ugly nickname game!

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Hm, we sense a faint Abyssal energy... An evil sorcerer must be lurking nearby, but they are well-hidden. If you encounter any suspicious outlanders, be sure to give them a robust interrogation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Suspicious outlanders? Wait, are you mocking us?

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Pah! How dare you cast aspersions on your ruler, heathen! You're just lucky that our servant has such vile taste in friends! Otherwise, we would beat you black and blue! And then purple! Then black again!

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: If you're not here to kiss my feet, then get out of my sight! Do not impede the work of the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw.

choices.text: So, little munchkin, whatcha doing up here?

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: That's "great sovereign" to you! You dare invite the wrath of the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw? You will burn in Turnfire for a thousand years for your blasphemy!

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Good luck, and stay safe! We'll wait right here.

talks.objective: Go back and find Huni and Toba

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Wow, you're back already! That was sooo fast!

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: I'm so glad that the babies are all right. Thank you both so much! Now we can finally go home and stop worrying about them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're welcome! Piece of cake.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: You're not from Natlan, right? 'Cause your clothes look different than ours. Hey, you must be tired after all that climbing. You should come take a rest at my house!

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Yeah, please come! I promise, you'll get a big Scions of the Canopy welcome! We love having guests, and you're really nice people — not like glasses guy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the sounds of it, "glasses guy" wasn't from Natlan either, right?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Uh-huh. Well, his clothes sure weren't... You know what, now that I think about it, there was something really fishy about him!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Maybe he was the suspicious outlander that Ajaw mentioned...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you tell us a little bit more about him?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Sure, if you're interested. Lemme think, how did the conversation go again...

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Please, Mister, I've told you so many stories already... When are you gonna help me find the baby Saurians?
Just one more story. One more, I swear. Why don't you tell me more about that ball of fire?
I heard that there was a huge, transparent ball of fire that used to burn... five hundred years ago? A thousand years ago? Maybe even further back than that.

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean Turnfire! That's where the ancient name "Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo" comes from!
Oh, wow, so it was the origin of an ancient name? That's impressive!

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Uh-huh! There's a story behind every ancient name. The legend goes that the Turnfire first appeared in the era of the Grand Alliance. It was used by the tyrant Och-Kan to rule over Natlan and oppress anyone who opposed him.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Turnfire is different from normal fire. If you get set on fire with it, you'll feel a horrible burning pain from behind you, but you won't die from it right away. And whatever you do, you mustn't turn back to look at it!
Why? What happens if you turn back?

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: As soon as you turn around, poof! You get burned to a crisp!
Well good golly gee... I mean, it's one thing to singe someone's clothes, but burning people alive? That is a big no-no in my book...

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Right? How nasty is it to burn someone from behind and not even let them turn around to look? Och-Kan really was an evil tyrant.
Yes, shocking behavior... Now let me guess — eventually, a valiant hero came to save the day? That's how these stories usually go.

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Good guess, Uncle Glasses! Seems like you really know your stuff. The hero was called Yupanqui. He's the ancestor of our tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. Yupanqui was friends with Och-Kan the tyrant and also Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon. He was working as an ordnance officer for the Grand Alliance at the time.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: He didn't like how Och-Kan was such a cruel tyrant. So he stole the Turnfire and threw it at the Och-Kan's army. The soldiers couldn't defend against it, and they all got turned to ash.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: And that's how our ancestor set our people free. But, just as he was about to leave the city, he thought he heard Och-Kan calling out to him from behind. It caught him off guard, and he turned around to look...

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: But Och-Kan wasn't there. All he saw was a city burned black, an army in ruins, and giant flames reaching up into the sky...

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: A split-second later, the flames he saw burst out from inside his eyes, and swallowed him up.

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: All it took was a single glance! As soon as he looked back, he was burned to a crisp.
The question is, was this the price he paid for stealing the Turnfire? Or the price of turning back?

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Nobody knows the answer. But the fire that consumed Yupanqui burned more fiercely than any other. It burned for a hundred days, until it burned a hole right through the ley lines!

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: And then, kshhh! The flame dropped into the deathly dark Night Kingdom, where it still burns to this day.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: The grown-ups say that it lights up the path that leads to the next life. But for the dead to be reborn, they have to accept the flames and be purified by the fire first.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: It's like a final look back at your life, where you have to answer for everything you did... Anyway, that's the story of Yupanqui's Turnfire.
Ahh... A fine parable indeed! So is it true? Is it really possible to find this fire in the Night Kingdom?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: I dunno... I think it's just a story.
Either way, I assume this name has been passed down in your tribe ever since?

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Sure has! It went to Burkina, the hero that we celebrate on Turnfire Night. But that was five hundred years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Yeah, and now it belongs to Kinich... So we often call him "Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo" Kinich.
Kinich, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Alright, Uncle Glasses, that's enough stories! Now, can you please go find the baby Saurians for us, like you promised?
Uhh... I would, but doesn't the legend of the Turnfire teach us not to look back? Let's not go dredging up the past.
Tell me more about this Kinich guy. One more story, I swear. Starting... now.
No? ...Careful Toba, you look dangerously close to cursing me out right now. Tut-tut, we can't have that. Cursing is for grown-ups only.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Uncle... You'd better not be trying to trick us... Or the Turnfire will get you when you die!
How would it get me if I'm outside of Natlan? Uncle Glasses isn't from here, you know. Unlike you.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Huh...?
Wait... Is that...?
...Alright, kiddos — I'm a man of my word. Two of my friends are on their way here and, uh... yeah. They'll help you out on my behalf.
Work them like dogs, okay? That's what they're here for. Don't go easy on them just for my sake.

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Really? ...Well, first can you tell us your name?

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: We met at the foot of this cliff, so... beneath the peaks... Let's go with "Sanka."

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Seriously...?

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: If you don't believe me, turn around and see for yourselves. They're right behind you.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Huh? Where...?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Wait... Uncle Sanka, where did you go!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, definitely a fishy character... It sounds like he was digging for info about the ancient names.

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Yeah! And not only that, but he betrayed us too! He'll pay for this!

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: All he got out of us were some stories, though. What's the worst that could happen?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hmm... {NICKNAME}, maybe we should go tell Kinich about this? Ajaw says he's investigating it, but he's a bit of a loose cannon. We probably shouldn't take him at his word.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Huh? You know Kinich?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Not very well. But we have met him before, and one time we had a meal together.

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Aw man, I'm so jealous! I've never even spoken to him. He's so cool! He's the Saurian-hunter, and he has a really awesome ancient name.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Me neither! I don't think my dad really likes him, though... He always tells me to stay away from him. Probably because of that little creep he always hangs out with. He's nasty. And he's so full of himself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, the creep who calls himself K'uhul Ajaw! Yeah, we've had the pleasure of meeting him too... He sure loves pushing people's buttons.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Exactly! I dunno why Kinich partnered up with him. Why didn't he pick me instead?

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Uh-oh! Huni, look how late it is! We've been out way too long... We'd better get home now, or we'll get yelled at!

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Yikes, you're right. Okay, well... this path here leads to our settlement. If you decide to visit, remember to come to my house!

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: If there's anything you need, my dad can help get it for you. Hope to see you soon!

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: We gotta run! Bye for now!

dialogues.speaker: Ponini
dialogues.text: Wah! Wah!

dialogues.speaker: Poggi
dialogues.text: Coo... Coo...
